title: How do we find 99 squared and 58 squared using minus signs?
description: Each number is written as a round number less a small number, and the square of eigh minus b gives its square in three pieces. Both answers are checked by multiplying in a different way.
teaching_notes: One idea: write the number as a round number less a small number, then use the square of eigh minus b. Same method as the square of side sixty video and the video on three squares with a minus sign.

source: Use the square of a difference to find the values of (a) 99² and (b) 58².
video_script.why: The child has expanded squares with a minus sign using letters. Here the two terms are numbers.
video_script.substitution: Write each number as a round number less a small number, put them in the pattern, add the three pieces, and check by multiplying another way.
video_script.anchor: ninety nine and fifty eight, each written as a round number less a small number
video_script.payoff_line: A round number less a small number makes the squares quick

final_answer.spoken: ninety nine squared is nine thousand eight hundred one, and fifty eight squared is three thousand three hundred sixty four

never_show: the middle term added instead of taken away
video_script.design: One idea: write the number as a round number less a small number, then use the square of eigh minus b. Uses the method of the square of side sixty video and the video on three squares with a minus sign. Each answer is checked by multiplying another way.

marks.mid: 2 × 100 × 1 = 200 is written with a minus sign before it

beats.colours: each piece in its own colour
narration: <bookmark mark='cut'/>Step one, write ninety nine as one hundred less one.
<bookmark mark='sq'/>The square of one hundred is ten thousand.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>Twice one hundred times one is two hundred, and it is taken away.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The square of one is one, and it is added.
<bookmark mark='tot'/>The total is nine thousand eight hundred one.

marks.mid: 2 × 60 × 2 = 240 is written with a minus sign before it

beats.colours: each piece in its own colour
narration: <bookmark mark='cut'/>Step two, write fifty eight as sixty less two.
<bookmark mark='sq'/>The square of sixty is three thousand six hundred.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>Twice sixty times two is two hundred forty, and it is taken away.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The square of two is four, and it is added.
<bookmark mark='tot'/>The total is three thousand three hundred sixty four.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Step three, check by multiplying in another way.
Ninety nine times one hundred is nine thousand nine hundred, less ninety nine.
<bookmark mark='b'/>That is nine thousand eight hundred one.
<bookmark mark='c'/>Fifty eight times sixty is three thousand four hundred eighty.
Take away fifty eight times two, which is one hundred sixteen.
<bookmark mark='d'/>That leaves three thousand three hundred sixty four.
